intro: Messi notched his eighth goal of the tournament but it took a last-gasp Fernández strike to bail Argentina out against Egypt, while over at Wimbledon, Muchová saved match point to break Gauff's heart in an absolute thriller. Elsewhere, Leclerc crashed Antonelli's party at Silverstone, and McClanahan shut the Yankees down as Tampa Bay stretched their AL East lead.

stories.headline: Messi at Eight: Argentina Survive Egypt Scare on Fernández's Last-Gasp Strike
stories.body: Argentina edged Egypt 3-2 with Enzo Fernández scoring in stoppage time, while Messi's goal pushed him to eight for the tournament. Eight goals at 38 years old at a World Cup is not a sentence that should be legal.

stories.headline: Mbappé Makes History, Then Limps Off Against Morocco
stories.body: Kylian Mbappé scored twice against Senegal to become France's all-time leading scorer, then left the Morocco quarterfinal with an apparent injury. France's biggest knockout game of the tournament and their best player is suddenly a question mark.

stories.headline: United Shell Out £50M for Andrey Santos as the Summer Spending Spree Hits Full Stride
stories.body: Manchester United agreed a £50 million deal with Chelsea for Brazilian midfielder Andrey Santos, while Atlético Madrid paid €40 million for Morten Hjulmand and Newcastle snapped up 18-year-old Ajax midfielder Sean Steur. The World Cup isn't even over and the transfer window is already unhinged.

stories.headline: Muchová Saves Match Point, Breaks Gauff's Heart in Wimbledon Thriller
stories.body: Karolína Muchová outlasted Coco Gauff 6-2, 1-6, 7-6(12-10) in a Wimbledon semifinal that nearly went the other way, saving a match point before closing it out in a tiebreak that lasted longer than most people's lunch breaks. With Linda Nosková already through on the other side, an all-Czech Wimbledon final is now a genuine possibility.

stories.headline: Djokovic Survives Five-Set War With Auger-Aliassime, Sinner Looms
stories.body: Novak Djokovic edged Félix Auger-Aliassime 7-6, 3-6, 6-3, 6-7, 7-6 in one of the tournament's longest matches, with the final two tiebreaks alone enough to age you visibly. Jannik Sinner is up next, so Djokovic gets approximately zero time to recover.

stories.headline: Osaka Stuns Sabalenka, Mboko Knee Injury Adds to Women's Draw Chaos
stories.body: Naomi Osaka knocked out world No. 1 contender Aryna Sabalenka at Wimbledon, blowing the women's draw wide open just as the business end of the tournament arrives. Meanwhile, Victoria Mboko — ranked No. 10 in the world — withdrew from the Canadian Open with a knee injury, giving the chaos a little extra seasoning.

stories.headline: Leclerc Crashes Antonelli's Party at Silverstone
stories.body: Charles Leclerc won the British Grand Prix under a safety-car finish, while championship leader Kimi Antonelli failed to score a single point. Antonelli still leads on 179 points, but his cushion over Russell and Hamilton just got a lot less comfortable.

stories.headline: Verstappen Calls Red Bull's Wing 'Super-Dangerous' After Crashing Out
stories.body: Max Verstappen didn't mince words after a rear-wing failure sent him out of the British GP while he was fighting for a podium, and Red Bull reportedly understood his anger. Nothing says team harmony like your driver describing your car as a safety hazard on race weekend.

stories.headline: FIA Boss Floats V8 Engines and Refuelling for 2031 — Yes, Really
stories.body: FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem is reportedly considering a return to V8 engines starting in 2031, potentially with refuelling and an independent engine supplier. Whether this is a bold vision or a nostalgia trip dressed up as a rulebook remains to be seen.

stories.headline: McClanahan Shuts Down the Yankees as Tampa Bay Widens AL East Lead
stories.body: Shane McClanahan threw 6 1/3 scoreless innings and Jonathan Aranda drove in all three runs as the Rays blanked New York 3-0, pushing their AL East lead further over a Yankees team that also got ejected out of another loss. Aaron Boone and bench coach Brad Ausmus were tossed in the process, which is one way to sum up New York's week.

stories.headline: Pete Crow-Armstrong Becomes MLB's First 20/20 Man of 2026
stories.body: Pete Crow-Armstrong hit his 20th homer and swiped his 20th bag this week, becoming the first player in MLB to hit the 20/20 mark this season — all while the Cubs were busy beating Baltimore 9-7 in a game that featured nine total home runs. Subtle week for the sport.

stories.headline: Red Sox Win Streak Hits 13 as Devers Walks It Off
stories.body: Boston's hot streak rolled to 13 games on Friday when Rafael Devers delivered a walk-off win to close out the week. The Red Sox have quietly become the most dangerous team nobody is talking about.

stories.headline: Mitchell Stays in Cleveland, Cashes Out to the Tune of $273 Million
stories.body: Donovan Mitchell locked in a 4-year, $273 million extension with the Cavaliers, making it very official that he is not going anywhere. Cleveland fans can breathe — their guy is home.

stories.headline: LeBron James Is Still a Free Agent and Somehow That's Not the Weirdest Story This Week
stories.body: LeBron is still weighing his options with interest from the 76ers, Warriors, Clippers, Raptors, and Timberwolves all in the mix heading into late July. Meanwhile, Mark Cuban is literally suing the Mavericks over the Luka trade, so the league is keeping itself busy.

stories.headline: Brunson's Wrist Is Fixed, Knicks Fans Can Exhale
stories.body: Jalen Brunson had wrist surgery but ESPN reports he'll be ready for the start of the season after returning to basketball activities this summer. New York dodged a big one.

stories.headline: Philly Throws a $90M Grenade at Anaheim: Leo Carlsson Offer Sheet Is Wild
stories.body: The Flyers slapped a 5-year, $90 million offer sheet on Anaheim's Leo Carlsson, giving the Ducks seven days to match or lose their guy. Philadelphia is clearly done being polite about rebuilding.

stories.headline: Hischier Stays, Nemec Leaves: New Jersey Had a Busy Week
stories.body: Nico Hischier locked in a 5-year, $58.5M extension to stay in New Jersey, while the Devils shipped Simon Nemec to Calgary, where he immediately landed a 5-year, $36.25M deal. One house cleaned up, one quietly emptied.

stories.headline: Toronto Drafts Gavin McKenna First Overall and Wastes Zero Time
stories.body: The Leafs took McKenna No. 1 overall and signed him to a 3-year entry-level contract before the confetti settled. Dallas' Jason Robertson, meanwhile, is still unsigned — so not everyone had a clean week.

stories.headline: Gotterup Goes Nuclear at John Deere, Shoots 62 to Claim Third Win of the Year
stories.body: Chris Gotterup closed with a blistering 62 to finish at -20 and win the John Deere Classic, his third PGA Tour victory this season. Three wins before August is the kind of thing that makes people start throwing around words like 'Player of the Year.'

stories.headline: Fox Birdies 18 to Steal The Open, Cameron Young Heartbroken Again
stories.body: Fox birdied the final hole to win The Open Championship by one shot over Cameron Young, who is quickly becoming the cruelest bridesmaid in major championship golf. One of these years, Young.

stories.headline: Aki Iwai Opens Evian Championship With a Scorching 63, Korda Nowhere to Be Found
stories.body: Aki Iwai fired an 8-under 63 to grab a two-shot lead in the opening round of the Evian Championship, while Nelly Korda had a rough start in her bid to bounce back after losing the KPMG. The leaderboard is wide open, but Iwai means business.

stories.headline: Lions CB Terrion Arnold Cut Loose — And Not Just From Detroit's Roster
stories.body: The Lions released Terrion Arnold last week, and now a Florida judge has set a $1 million bond against him in a kidnapping case involving allegations he orchestrated the abduction and pistol-whipping of three people. From starting CB to free agent to bond hearing is quite the offseason arc.

stories.headline: Kyle Pitts Gets Paid in Atlanta — Three Years, $54 Million to Stay a Falcon
stories.body: The Falcons locked up tight end Kyle Pitts on a three-year, $54 million extension that keeps him in Atlanta through 2028. After the injury-riddled stretch Pitts has had, Atlanta is betting he's finally ready to live up to that first-round hype.

stories.headline: Camps Are Open and Half the League Is Limping Back to Health
stories.body: Training camp is officially underway across the NFL, with Bo Nix, George Kittle, Nick Bosa, Travis Hunter, and Malik Nabers among the notable names returning from injuries — Hunter is expected to be fully cleared. Meanwhile, the Jets landed Minkah Fitzpatrick via trade and Trey Hendrickson inked a four-year, $112 million deal, so the offseason spending isn't quite done yet.

stories.headline: NCAA Blows Up the Eligibility Rulebook With New 5-Year Model
stories.body: The NCAA approved a five-season-in-five-year model for Division I athletes and voted to eliminate redshirts and waivers from the eligibility equation. College sports just got a little less confusing, which is honestly its own kind of miracle.

stories.headline: Sorsby Drops Lawsuit, Gets His Injunction, Will Play — What a Week
stories.body: Brendan Sorsby's eligibility saga wrapped up with an injunction securing his right to play after Cincinnati accused Texas Tech of tampering and the NCAA sent an inquiry letter. The NFL also confirmed there will be no supplemental draft, so Sorsby is officially a college football problem again.

stories.headline: Ohio State Lands Jett Harrison, Because One Harrison Apparently Wasn't Enough
stories.body: The Buckeyes added 5-star receiver Jett Harrison — yes, Marvin Harrison Jr.'s brother — to their 2027 recruiting class. Ohio State's wide receiver room is becoming a family reunion.
